<reason>Side A wins by demonstrating that Side B's proposed alternative—requiring secured beds before acceptance—concedes the principle that recruitment must be constrained by housing capacity, while arguing that only an external public cap avoids the conflict of interest of universities judging their own limits. A also effectively resolves the housing-market contradiction via the "sequence" argument (purpose-built absorption followed by local-market overflow) and provides concrete criteria for the "severe" trigger that B fails to fully counter.</reason>
